rows.rationale: KA-C5-006 (effective 2025-12-01) supersedes KA-C5-001 (effective 2023-08-05), raising check meter threshold to 50kWp. | Clause states installations up to 150kW are deemed feasible; 45kWp system should pass technical feasibility, not be rejected. | Check meter required only for capacity >50kWp; 45kWp system does not require check meter.

Proposed capacity is 45 kWp, which is below the 50 kWp threshold requiring a check meter, so this clause does not justify rejection. | System is 45 kW (under 150 kW) and deemed feasible per cl-4-note-ii; cumulative 95 kW on 100 kVA transformer is within 80% limit, so no technical infeasibility.

The clause makes check meters mandatory only for systems >20 kW; this system is exactly 20 kWp, so check meter is optional, not required. | GJ-C3-003 (effective 2020-01-22) amends GJ-C3-001 (effective 2016-06-17); the 2020 amendment should be cited as the in-force rule for 2025 application.

Proposed capacity is exactly 20 kW, so check meter is optional per the rule, yet application lacks one and generator approved without flagging this compliance gap. | The cited clause concerns check meter requirements, not approval criteria; it cannot alone justify full application approval.

The cited clause describes SDO verification process, but Technical Feasibility Outcome is 'Not communicated by the licensee', so approval cannot be granted yet. | 60kWp capacity ≤150kW qualifies as deemed feasible under this rule, but generator failed to cite this applicable provision.

The cited clause is effective from 2025-12-01, but the application date is 2026-04-30; however, the application is still at 'Technical Feasibility' stage with outcome 'Not communicated by the licensee', so approval decision is premature. | The SDO must verify technical feasibility and issue intimation letter per KA-C5-001#cl-26, but feasibility outcome has not been communicated yet.

GJ-C3-003 (effective 2020-01-22) amended cl-13.5, replacing 0.2s requirement with 1.0/0.5S class; original regulation superseded before application date 2025-09-03. | The amended meter accuracy requirements from GJ-C3-003 should have been cited as the governing rule.

The cited clause requires Net Meter accuracy of 0.5S or better, but application shows Net Meter at 0.2S which satisfies this; however, approval cannot be based solely on meter accuracy compliance without verifying capacity limits. | System capacity (8 kWp) exceeds sanctioned load (5 kW), which typically requires load enhancement approval under GERC regulations before interconnection approval.

DL-C3-009 (effective 2024-04-01) amended clause 3.8, superseding the original 5-5000 kW limits before the 2024-08-04 application date. | The amended rule allows GNM capacity up to 5x sanctioned load (max 10 MW); 12 MW exceeds 10 MW cap, but correct rule was not cited.

Sanctioned Load is 3000 kW; 5 times equals 15,000 kW (15 MW), capped at 10 MW; proposed 12,000 kWp (12 MW) exceeds 10 MW cap but generator's rejection reasoning appears to misapply the rule without showing this calculation.

UP-C3-001 (2015 Regulations) was superseded by UP-C3-002 (2019 Regulations) effective 2019-01-04, before the 2023-08-08 application date. | Proposed 1.00 kWp is within 100% of 2.0 kW sanctioned load and meets minimum 1 kWp requirement; rejection is unsupported.

The cited clause only establishes capacity limits; it does not authorize approval or address subsidy eligibility, workflow stage, or interconnection mode requirements. | No subsidy rules were cited or evaluated despite subsidy being a standard component of rooftop solar applications.
The clause requires check meters for systems >20kW but does not mandate rejection; the meter can be installed during the meter installation stage where the application currently sits.
The clause mandates check meters for systems >20 kW, but this is an equipment specification issue, not grounds for outright rejection—the applicant can still install the required check meter.

KA-C5-001#cl-15 (17.5 kW threshold) is superseded by KA-C5-006#cl-18 (50 kWp threshold) effective 2025-12-01, which was in force on application date 2026-02-16. | The applicable rule requires check meter only for systems >50 kWp; the 80 kWp system requires a check meter, but this newer rule was not cited.
The clause mandates check meters only for systems >20 kW; this 12 kWp system is ≤20 kW, making check meters optional, not mandatory.
Check meters are mandatory only for systems >20 kW; this 12 kWp system is ≤20 kW, so check meter is optional, not required.

DL-C3-004#cl-9.2b was superseded by DL-C3-015 (effective 2026-01-20), which allows twice per financial year, not once. | Under amended rule, 2 changes per year are permitted with 2 months notice; applicant made 2 changes with 3 months notice, so compliant.

The rule allows adding connections twice per year with 2-month notice; applicant has made 2 changes but gave 3-month notice, so a third addition should be rejected, but this is actually the third change, not second—however the rejection reasoning misreads the rule as prohibiting when limits are met with proper notice.

DL-C3-004#cl-3.8 was superseded by DL-C3-009#cl-3.8 (Fifth Amendment) effective 2024-04-01, before the application date of 2025-03-14. | The applicable rule limits GNM capacity to 5x sanctioned load (120kW × 5 = 600kW max); 90kWp complies but this rule was not cited.

The cited clause governs maximum capacity limits (up to 5x sanctioned load), but the generator failed to verify that 90 kWp ≤ 600 kW (5 × 120 kW) and did not record any computed values. | Clause 3.8 sets capacity limits but does not constitute a standalone approval basis; other eligibility and technical interconnection rules were not considered.

TN-C5-002 (effective 2021-10-22) supersedes net feed-in rules for commercial consumers before application date 2022-09-24. | Commercial LB-V consumers are governed by net billing/net feed-in under Order No.8/2021, which was not cited.

The cited clause (effective 2021-10-22) was not in force on the application date (2022-09-24 uses 2019 policy for LT Commercial; TN-C5-001 is applicable). | TN-C5-001#cl-2 limits LT net feed-in capacity to 100% of sanctioned demand (150 kW), and this governing rule was not cited.

DL-C3-009 (effective 2024-04-01) is superseded by DL-C3-015 (effective 2026-01-20) which was in force on application date 2026-09-06. | The applicable 2025 amendment with updated 110 MW threshold for BRPL was not cited; cumulative 50 MW is within the new limit. | SLD waiver applies to 11kV and below; this project connects at 33 kV, so the cited clause threshold is irrelevant to rejection.

Clause 3.6 concerns SLD/network augmentation cost waiver up to 110 MW for BRPL; cumulative capacity is 50 MW (under limit), and this clause does not provide grounds for application rejection. | The SLD waiver applies only to 11kV and below networks, but this project connects at 33 kV, so the waiver clause is irrelevant to rejection at portal registration stage.

DL-C3-009 (Fifth Amendment, 2024) is superseded by DL-C3-015 (Seventh Amendment, effective 2026-01-20), which raises TPDDL's SLD waiver cap to 100 MW. | The applicable Seventh Amendment (effective 2026-01-20) with 100 MW cap for TPDDL was not considered; at 105 MW cumulative, rejection may still apply but under the current rule.

The cited clause sets TPDDL's SLD waiver cap at 100 MW; cumulative capacity is 105 MW, so only SLD waiver is lost—not grounds for outright rejection of the application. | The clause governs SLD/network augmentation cost waiver eligibility, not portal registration rejection criteria.

UP-C3-001 (2015 Regulations) was superseded by UP-C3-002 (2019 Regulations) effective 2019-01-04, before the application date of 2023-09-16. | The applicable 2019 regulation allows up to 75% DT capacity (120 kW for 160 kVA), and 125 kW cumulative would pass under correct threshold. | Even under the cited 15% limit (24 kW), existing 110 kW already exceeds it; the decision's arithmetic context is inconsistent.

Resultant cumulative capacity 125 kW is 78.1% of 160 kVA DT, exceeding 75% threshold, but the 15 kWp addition itself could be partially approved or the application should clarify capacity reduction options rather than outright rejection.

DL-C3-009 (effective 2024-04-01) amended clause 3.8, superseding the original 5-5000 kW limits before the 2024-06-28 application date. | Amended rule allows GNM capacity up to 5x sanctioned load (max 10MW); 600 kWp ≤ 5×100kW=500kW threshold needs verification, but rejection basis is wrong.

Proposed 600 kWp is within 5x sanctioned load (5×100kW=500kW capacity limit applies to participating consumer's load, but 600kWp DC may convert to ≤500kW AC; regardless, max 10MW cap is satisfied and rejection reasoning misapplies the rule).

DL-C3-004#cl-3.8 was superseded by DL-C3-009#cl-3.8 (Fifth Amendment, effective 2024-04-01), which applies to the 2024-05-22 application date. | The amended rule limits ground-mounted GNM capacity to 5× sanctioned load (500 kW max here), but 600 kWp was proposed; this rule was not considered.

Clause 3.8 applies to Ground Mounted RE Systems, but the application is for rooftop solar, not ground-mounted. | Even if applicable, 600 kWp exceeds 5x sanctioned load (5×100kW=500kW), violating the cited capacity limit.

Cl-26 describes SDO's verification process, not approval criteria; Technical Feasibility Outcome is 'Not communicated' so approval is premature. | Installations ≤150kW are deemed feasible per KA-C5-006, which is newer (2025-12-01) and should have been cited.

The cited clause establishes deemed feasibility for <150kW installations but does not authorize final approval; Technical Feasibility has not been communicated by HESCOM per portal status. | SDO must issue intimation letter confirming technical feasibility before approval; this procedural step is incomplete as feasibility outcome is 'Not communicated'.

DL-C3-015 (effective 2026-01-20) supersedes DL-C3-006#cl-3.2, extending VNM to all consumers in NCT Delhi. | Clause 3.8 governs capacity limits for ground-mounted systems, not VNM eligibility criteria. | Current rule allows VNM for all Delhi consumers; application should not be rejected on category grounds.

DL-C3-015#cl-3.2 extends VNM to ALL consumers in Delhi, so citing it as grounds for rejection contradicts the clause's permissive content. | Proposed 150 kWp exceeds 5× sanctioned load (5×20=100 kW) per cl-3.8, which should be the actual rejection ground but was not properly reasoned.

GJ-C3-003#cl-6.2 was amended by GJ-C3-004 (effective 2022-05-31), which supersedes the 50% limit for captive consumers. | This clause explicitly states 'No capacity restrictions upto sanctioned load' for captive consumers, supporting approval not rejection.

Clause 6.2c-ii removes capacity restrictions for captive consumers, but applicant is HTP-I Industrial under net metering for captive use, not explicitly a 'captive consumer' category under Gujarat regulations. | For non-residential, non-MSME consumers, capacity limit is 50% of sanctioned load (50 kW), but proposed 80 kWp exceeds this limit and rule was not considered.

The cited clause makes check meters mandatory only for systems >20 kW; this 18 kWp system is ≤20 kW, so check meter is optional, not a basis for approval. | GJ-C3-003 (effective 2020-01-22) amends GJ-C3-001 (2016); the 2020 amendment should govern for a 2025 application.

The clause makes check meters mandatory only for systems >20 kW; this 18 kWp system is ≤20 kW, so check meter is optional and cannot block approval. | Cited rule governs check meter requirements but does not justify approving/rejecting the application itself.

KA-C5-001#cl-15 (effective 2023-08-05) requiring check meter >17.5kW is superseded by KA-C5-006#cl-18 (effective 2025-12-01) requiring check meter >50kWp. | 30kWp system is below 50kWp threshold in current regulation KA-C5-006#cl-18, so check meter is not required and application should be approved without this concern.

Clause requires check meter for systems >50kWp, but the 30kWp system lacks a check meter and this is irrelevant to approval since it's below threshold. | KA-C5-001#cl-15 requires check meter for SRTPV >17.5kW; 30kWp system exceeds this but no check meter is provided.

GJ-C3-003 (effective 2020-01-22) amended the 65% limit to 100%, superseding GJ-C3-001#cl-5-proviso before the 2025 application date. | Under amended regulations, 85 kW cumulative capacity does not exceed 100 kVA transformer capacity (100%), so rejection is incorrect.
Resultant cumulative capacity (85 kW) exceeds the 100 kVA transformer capacity limit, so application should be rejected, not approved.

GJ-C3-003 amended the 65% limit to 100% effective 2020-01-22, superseding the cited clause before the 2025-01-17 application date. | The applicable 100% transformer capacity limit under the 2020 amendment was not applied; 70kW cumulative is within 100kVA limit.
Resultant cumulative capacity 70 kW exceeds 100% of 100 kVA transformer capacity, so application should be rejected, not approved.

The 9kWp system is under 150kW and deemed feasible per KA-C5-006#cl-4-note-ii (effective 2025-12-01), which supersedes the SDO verification process cited. | Technical feasibility outcome is 'Not communicated by the licensee', so approval cannot be justified when verification is incomplete.

Clause effective date is 2025-12-01, but application date is 2026-06-06; however, the document KA-C5-006 is applicable only from December 2025 onwards and the older KA-C5-001 (effective 2023-08-05) requires SDO verification per clause 26. | Technical feasibility requires SDO verification and intimation letter per KA-C5-001#cl-26; feasibility outcome is 'Not communicated' so approval is premature.

KA-C5-006#cl-18 (effective 2025-12-01) supersedes KA-C5-001#cl-15, raising check meter threshold to 50kWp. | Application date 2026-01-13 requires KA-C5-006#cl-18 which mandates check meter only for >50kWp; 35kWp system should be approved without check meter requirement.

KA-C5-001#cl-15 requires check meter for SRTPV systems >17.5kW; at 35kWp, check meter is required but not provided. | Cited clause exempts systems ≤50kWp from check meter, but older KA-C5-001#cl-15 (still in force) requires it above 17.5kW.

GJ-C3-003 (effective 2020-01-22) amended clause 13.5, replacing 0.2s accuracy requirement with 1.0 class for Solar Generation Meter. | Application's Solar Generation Meter is 1.0 class accuracy, which complies with amended regulation requiring 1.0 class or better.

System is 25 kWp (>20 kW), so Check Meter is mandatory per cl-13.5-check, but generator cited this rule without noting the missing Check Meter as the actual violation. | Solar Generation Meter is 1.0 class and Net Meter is 0.5S, both meeting the 1.0/0.5S requirement; rejection on meter accuracy is unsupported by evidence.

The clause permits installation up to 100% of sanctioned demand (8.0 kW), but the proposal requests Net Billing mode, not Net Feed-in, so the 8 kW limit under this specific clause may not apply. | For Net Billing mode, TN-C5-002 allows all consumer categories irrespective of sanctioned load limits, which was not considered by the generator.
The cited clause permits systems up to 999 kW for net billing; the 10 kWp proposal is well within the 8 kW sanctioned load limit, so rejection is unsupported.

DL-C3-006 (2020) is superseded by DL-C3-015 (2025) which amended Guideline 3(2) effective 2026-01-20, before the application date of 2026-06-23. | Even under old rules, VNM applied to domestic/charitable institutions, but applicant is NDLT Non-Domestic tariff with commercial shops, not an eligible category. | The current applicable VNM guideline (DL-C3-015) should have been cited instead of the superseded 2020 amendment.

VNM is applicable for all consumers, but the proposed 120 kWp system exceeds 100% of sanctioned load (30 kW), violating capacity limits not addressed. | Non-Domestic (commercial) consumers are not listed among eligible VNM categories in the 2020 amendment defining applicability. | No rule cited for system capacity limits relative to sanctioned load; 120 kWp exceeds 30 kW sanctioned load by 400%.

GJ-C3-003 (effective 2020-01-22) amended the 65% limit to 100% of transformer capacity, superseding GJ-C3-001#cl-5-proviso before the 2024 application date. | The amended regulation allowing 100% transformer capacity should have been applied; 55kW is within 100kVA limit.

Resultant cumulative capacity (55 kW) exceeds transformer capacity (100 kVA), so the 100% limit is satisfied; however, GJ-C3-001#cl-5-proviso (65% limit = 65 kW) was superseded only partially, and 55 kW still passes both, but the application proposes 5 kWp on 3 kW sanctioned load, violating typical capacity limits not addressed. | Generator did not verify that proposed system capacity (5 kWp) exceeds sanctioned load (3 kW), which typically requires load enhancement approval under net metering regulations.

UP-C3-001 (2015 Regulations) was superseded by UP-C3-002 (2019 Regulations) effective 2019-01-04, before the application date of 2023-04-19. | Under 2019 rules, capacity limit is 100% of connected load (4 kW); proposed 5 kWp exceeds this, but generator cited wrong regulation version.
Proposed 5 kWp exceeds 100% of 4 kW sanctioned load, but correct remedy is capacity reduction, not outright rejection; also, connected load equals sanctioned load here, so 4 kWp would be permissible.

DL-C3-009 (Fifth Amendment) is superseded by DL-C3-015 (Seventh Amendment) effective 2026-01-20, which was in force on application date 2026-04-11. | The applicable Seventh Amendment raises BRPL's cumulative capacity threshold to 110 MW, but this rule was not cited by the generator. | Cumulative capacity including this project is 95 MW, which exceeds the 75 MW threshold in the cited outdated rule but is within the 110 MW limit in the current rule; approval reasoning is based on wrong threshold.

The cited clause only waives SLD charges; it does not authorize approval of systems exceeding sanctioned load (400 kWp vs 100 kW sanctioned load limit). | Generator failed to consider capacity limits requiring proposed solar capacity to not exceed sanctioned load for net metering eligibility.

GJ-C3-003#cl-6.2 applies to Residential/MSME consumers; HTP-I Industrial tariff category is neither, so 50% cap rule doesn't apply here. | Clause permits no capacity restriction for captive consumers, but application is for net metering non-residential industrial, not explicitly captive under this provision. | Net metering capacity limit (1kW-1000kW) and sanctioned load alignment for non-residential industrial consumers were not properly evaluated.

TN-C5-001 (effective 2019-05-10) is superseded by TN-C5-002 (effective 2021-10-22) for net billing applications, which was in force on the application date 2022-08-18. | Net billing consumers under TN-C5-002 are not limited to 100% of sanctioned load; this applicable rule allowing higher capacity was not considered.

The cited clause permits systems up to 999 kW and the 6 kWp proposal is within this limit; rejection is unsupported. | TN-C5-001#cl-2 limits capacity to 100% of sanctioned load (4 kW), but the 6 kWp proposal exceeds this threshold and was not cited.

UP-C3-001 (2015 Regulations) was superseded by UP-C3-002 (2019 Regulations) effective 2019-01-04, before the application date of 2023-07-04. | The applicable 2019 regulation allows 75% transformer capacity (75 kW for 100 kVA), and 78 kW cumulative is within limit, so rejection is unsupported.

Existing 72 kW + proposed 6 kW = 78 kW is 78% of 100 kVA, exceeding 75% limit by only 3 kW; however, the generator incorrectly stated the root cause—the limit is 75 kW (75% of 100 kVA), but 72 kW already violates this before adding 6 kW, so partial approval or correct arithmetic explanation was needed.

DL-C3-004#cl-9.2b was superseded by DL-C3-015 (effective 2026-01-20) which allows two changes per financial year, not one. | Under amended rules, applicant's 1 prior change plus this request equals 2, which is within the permitted limit of twice per financial year.

Clause allows two VNM modifications per year; applicant has made only 1 prior change, so adding another is permitted and rejection is unwarranted. | Clause requires 2 months advance notice but applicant gave only 1 month, which should be the stated rejection reason, not exceeding modification count.

Application was submitted 2023-12-05 under Phase II, but the amended rule IN-C1-001#cl-annex1-ii-amended extends CFA eligibility for Phase II claims until 31.12.2025, superseding the October 2024 deadline. | Generator failed to consider the amended clause allowing Phase II CFA claims until 31.12.2025; CFA claim received 2026-02-16 exceeds even this extended deadline.
The clause states Phase II claims are admissible if received till 31.12.2025; CFA claim received 2026-02-16 is after this deadline, but the generator's garbled citation misrepresents the rule text.

DL-C3-009 (effective 2024-04-01) is superseded by DL-C3-015 (effective 2026-01-20), which was in force on application date 2026-05-18. | Under current rules, TPDDL's SLD waiver cap is 100 MW, but cumulative capacity is 120 MW, exceeding the threshold and disqualifying the waiver.

Cumulative TPDDL capacity is 120 MW, exceeding the 100 MW threshold for SLD waiver under DL-C3-015#cl-3.6, so the waiver condition is not met. | The cited clause concerns SLD waiver eligibility, not overall project approval; approval decision requires additional regulatory basis not cited.

GJ-C3-001 (2016) was amended by GJ-C3-003 (2020), which changed Solar Meter accuracy requirement from 0.2s to 1.0 class; the cited 0.2s rule is superseded. | Under the amended regulation, Solar Meter requires 1.0 class accuracy, but the proposal specifies 0.5S class, which does not comply with the current requirement.

The regulation requires Solar Meter accuracy of 1.0 class, but the EPC proposal shows Solar Generation Meter at 0.5S class, which is better and compliant, however the cited rule alone does not constitute grounds for full application approval. | Generator did not verify capacity limits, net metering eligibility, or other mandatory approval criteria beyond meter accuracy class.

KA-C5-006#cl-4-note-ii supersedes this: installations ≤150kW are deemed feasible without SDO verification, making cl-26 inapplicable. | 40kWp system is under 150kW threshold, so deemed feasibility rule applies but was not cited. | Technical feasibility outcome is 'Not communicated'; approval cannot be granted when feasibility is pending.

The cited clause establishes deemed feasibility but does not authorize final approval; the application is still at Technical Feasibility stage with outcome 'Not communicated by the licensee', so approval is premature. | The SDO must verify technical feasibility and issue intimation letter before approval; this procedural requirement was not considered despite application being pending at that workflow stage.

The October 2024 deadline was superseded by IN-C1-001#cl-annex1-ii-amended extending the deadline to 31.12.2025; the CFA claim received 2026-01-15 misses this extended deadline, not the cited rule. | Generator failed to cite the amended clause extending Phase II claims deadline to 31.12.2025, which is the applicable rule for this application date.

The clause states Phase II applications are admissible for CFA if claim received till 31.12.2025; the CFA claim was received 2026-01-15, after this deadline, but the generator's garbled citation misinterprets the rule and the application date (2023-09-04) predates the submission date shown (2026-02-14), creating inconsistency. | This clause confirms Phase II applications submitted before 13 Feb 2024 remain eligible for CFA, which applies here (submitted 2023-09-04), but was not considered in the rejection reasoning.

DL-C3-006 (2020) was superseded by DL-C3-015 (effective 2026-01-20), which expanded VNM to all Delhi consumers. | This clause sets capacity limits for ground-mounted systems, not VNM eligibility criteria. | The applicable 2025 amendment allows VNM for all NCT Delhi consumers, making domestic applicants eligible.

The cited clause explicitly states VNM is applicable for all Delhi consumers, which supports approval, not rejection. | 200 kWp capacity exceeds 5x sanctioned load (5×30kW=150kW), violating the capacity limit—this rule should cause rejection but was not properly explained as root cause.
